text:
jun_park: Quick postmortem note: discovered why server-side idempotency dedupe was missing for some uploads from Android SDK. Not a duplicate client request; server saw two different canonical signatures because of chunked encoding vs content-length. Repro + notes below.

maria_g: interesting. did the client send two different idempotency headers or the same header but server canonicalized differently?

jun_park: same header value bytes, but our SDK signs the whole request canonical string that includes Content-Length if present. When the client switched to chunked transfer (streaming RequestBody), Content-Length is absent, so server canonicalization used `transfer-encoding: chunked` in the string and produced a different signature. Proxy in front rewrote chunking headers in one case. Result: signature mismatch -> server accepted both.

sam_k: so two failure modes: (A) header same but signature input differs because transfer metadata differs; (B) some SDKs (Java vs Kotlin builders) attach idempotency header at different interceptor phases, and proxies may reorder or remove non-safe headers. We need a robust approach.

jun_park: my proposal: 1) canonicalize idempotency signature to exclude transport-layer fluctuating headers (Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding) and only include stable fields (method, path, sorted stable headers like our idempotency-key, body hash). 2) change SDK to compute a body SHA256 hash on the client for the signature (or include a body digest header) so server can verify dedupe even if chunking differs. 3) ship a small helper that computes a deterministic canonical string and HMACs it with client secret for server-side verification.

maria_g: hashing body on client for large streams is heavy. Could we instead compute a cheap rolling hash (e.g., SHA256 of first N bytes + length) for very large streams and mark as approximate? Server can accept approximate-dedupe for large files and use content-addressing if needed. Also provide a ReplayableRequestBody helper so users can opt-in to exact body hashing if they want strict dedupe.

sam_k: agree. Also important: ensure Java SDK and Kotlin SDK use same canonicalization logic. We had a parity bug where Kotlin's interceptor lowercased headers before signing while Java SDK preserved case. Add cross-language unit tests that assert identical canonical strings for same inputs.

jun_park: implemented a prototype TokenIdempotencySigner in sampleapp: it computes body digest header `X-Redwood-Body-SHA256` for small bodies or stores a temp-file cached digest for streams > threshold (opt-in). It then builds canonical string: `<method>
<path>
<header:idempotency-key>
<body-sha256>` and HMACs it. Server change PR will skip transport headers and verify HMAC + body-sha if present.

maria_g: sounds good. Short-term mitigation: document that auth/interceptor ordering matters: place idempotency header as early as possible (before network interceptors) and avoid adding it conditionally after fallback logic. Add test that simulates proxy reordering and chunked transfer.

sam_k: devex-bot: created RED-DEVEX-4202 with prototype signer + sampleapp demo + server verification PR link <https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-DEVEX-4202>. Please add cross-sdk tests for canonicalization parity.

jun_park: I'll open a PR with: (A) TokenIdempotencySigner utility (opt-in in SDK), (B) ReplayableRequestBody helper docs, (C) test matrix Java/Kotlin parity, (D) docs note about chunked vs content-length and proxies. Will also add migration note for existing customers.

maria_g: thanks. Also note that enabling body hashing for all uploads may impact battery/network on mobile; make it opt-in with sensible defaults.

sam_k: agreed. After PR land, we'll update the onboarding guide to recommend: idempotency + body-digest header for non-idempotent endpoints, ReplayableRequestBody for strict dedupe, and avoid adding idempotency headers late in interceptor chain.

jun_park: PR up in a bit. tagging infra + api-security for review :thumbsup:

devex-bot: Linked issue RED-DEVEX-4202 and created draft PR for TokenIdempotencySigner and parity tests.
